suggestions.title: Weigh in Friday and Saturday — Thursday's 161.1 is the lowest read on file, and one morning can't confirm itself

rationale.science: Day-to-day scale weight moves with water, not fat — sodium and carbohydrate alone can swing it a pound or more overnight — so a single morning is a data point, not a verdict; the trend only moves when consecutive clean mornings agree. (Juraschek 2020, DASH-Sodium; Powers 2003)
rationale.data: Thu 9/03 read 161.1 — lowest in the file (prior low 161.8 on 8/20) and 2.2 lb under your 163.3 trend. Wed 9/02 had no read. Your app damped it as a spike; so did I. Your own day-to-day noise is ±1.46 lb.
rationale.relationship: Two mornings at or under the low 162s pull the trend down most of a pound and settle the August fat-or-water question for good; two mornings back near 163 file Thursday as water leaving. Either way the rate — which neither your app nor I can price on a half-blank window — comes back on the board. My lean: confirm, about 60/40.

suggestions.predict: Both mornings logged: the trend lands 162.5–163.0 by Saturday if the reads confirm, or holds near 163.3 if they don't — I'm calling confirm. Neither morning logged by Sunday 9/06: this files as a miss on the ask, not a read on you, and the card retires.

suggestions.title: Keep logging food forward — three days in, the maintenance math is already settling; give it four more

rationale.science: Consistent self-monitoring is the strongest single predictor of fat-loss success; gaps, not metabolism, explain most stalls. (Alhassan 2008; Burke 2011)
rationale.data: 8/31 2,150 · 9/01 2,275 · 9/02 2,300 kcal; protein 175 / 175 / 200 g; steps 20,000 / 19,500 / 19,000. Across those days the app's maintenance estimate moved 2,429 → 2,353 → 2,321 and its range tightened from ~270 to ~200 kcal wide (36 matched days). 9/03 has no food yet.
rationale.relationship: Every matched day reprices the fit — it moved 76, then 32, then 0. The first few days make it jump; the next few make it settle. The band is the app's call; the only input you control is whether the day exists.

suggestions.predict: Five of the seven days 9/02–9/08 logged with food: the range stays ~200 kcal wide or tighter and no single day moves the estimate more than ~50 kcal. Fewer than three logged by 9/09: this files as a miss on the ask, not on you.

suggestions.title: Last call: tap Approve or Dismiss on one card — you were in the app four days this week and no card was touched

rationale.science: Only graded predictions sharpen a model; an untested proposal teaches nothing either way. This is about the feedback loop, not your body.
rationale.data: Your decision log ends 8/14 (24 entries). Contact days since: 8/31, 9/01, 9/02, 9/03 — reads, three food days and a full session all carried by the sync. Every card issued since 8/14 is undecided.
rationale.relationship: A working pipe carried everything except decisions. If the buttons work and you're choosing not to tap, fine — I stop counting silence against my record. If they don't work, that's a bug worth one line to the developer. One tap, even Dismiss, answers it. This is a hunch about the app, not a read on you.

suggestions.predict: Any decision dated 9/02 or later in the log by tomorrow's run: the channel works and the freeze was a choice — I stop grading non-decisions. Nothing by 9/05: I report the button as likely broken in the brief and retire this card.
